items.desc: A path traversal flaw was found in ansible-core. When installing a collection with ansible-galaxy collection install, the install destination directory is derived from the namespace and name fields declared inside the collection artifact's own metadata, which are not validated as well-formed collection identifiers or checked for path containment. A malicious collection artifact -- delivered as a local file, a remote URL, a source directory, a git repository, or as a dependency -- can use a crafted name value to redirect the install destination outside the configured collections path, causing ansible-galaxy to delete an existing directory writable by the invoking user and then write attacker-controlled files to that location.

This vulnerability affected supported GitHub Enterprise Server releases prior to 3.23 and was fixed…

items.desc: A flaw was found in CRI-O. When the optional Linux LinkLogs feature is enabled, the host pod log directory is bind-mounted into a pod emptyDir and is intended to be read-only, but Linux ignores MS_RDONLY on the initial bind and the CRI mount stays writable. A non-privileged UID 0 container can place a symlink at a future kubelet log path so that privileged conmon later appends attacker-controlled log data to an existing host file. This is an append-only host integrity issue, not universal remote code execution; LinkLogs is not enabled by default.

An explicit role "name" taken from a role's meta/requirements.yml is used to construct the on-disk installation path without validating that the resulting destination stays within the selected roles directory. items.desc:
IO::Socket::SSL::PublicSuffix versions through 2.099 for Perl allow code injection via a fetched list line that closes the built-in data heredoc when update_self_from_url rewrites the module's source.

The rewrite copies the module's source down to the built-in list's heredoc and appends each fetched line below it. Nothing checks that a line looks like a domain. A line that is not a comment loses only what follows a `//` and its trailing whitespace, so a line reading END_BUILTIN_DATA is appended as it stands and ends the data block in the rewritten file. Every fetched line after it is Perl.

Arbitrary Perl runs in every process that loads IO::Socket::SSL, which loads this module unconditionally, until the file is reinstalled. items.title: IO::Socket::SSL::PublicSuffix versions through 2.099 for Perl let an on-path attacker choose the installed public suffix list…
items.ai: 暂无 CVSS 评分。暂无公开 POC，按常规补丁窗口安排。 影响版本：详见公告。
items.desc:
IO::Socket::SSL::PublicSuffix versions through 2.099 for Perl let an on-path attacker choose the installed public suffix list because update_self_from_url fetches it over cleartext HTTP with no integrity check.

Called with no argument, as the module's documentation shows, the updater fetches the list from the `http://` address in the URL constant and checks only that the request succeeded, with no signature or digest over the response. The lines that come back are written into the module's own source file as the built-in list.

An attacker on the network path when the updater runs chooses the suffix boundary the module reports to every caller on the host, and that answer persists in the installed module until it is reinstalled. Dropping one rule makes the hostname check in IO::Socket::SSL accept a wildcard certificate that spans the whole public suffix that rule named.
